King Muhammad bin Nayef walks swiftly into the King Abdualaziz City of Science and Technology Space Center. He is approached by an engineer. "Your Highness, hello! I was excited to hear that you were planning on building another satellite! Saudi Arabia is really gaining a major presence in space!"

"Yes," The Saudi King said with a small laugh. "I need to speak to the lead engineer."

"Of course, my king! Follow me." The engineer led King Muhammad to a sterile white room containing a man sitting behind a desk surrounded by file cabinets. The man was busy typing away on his computer, and didn't notice the king and engineer enter. The engineer cleared his throat to get the man's attention.

"What is it?" The man said with disdain. "I'm bu-" He stopped short seeing the king. "Oh! King Muhammad bin Nayef! I am so terribly sorry! I am Chief Engineer Fahad Hazazi." Fahad stood and shook King Muhammad's hand. "I heard about the new satellite you wish built! I have to admit, we are all very excited to see our great nation moving further into space!"

"That is actually what I have come to speak to you about." The king said with a smile. Noticing that the engineer who led him here was still standing beside him, he looked his way and gave a small cough. Taking the hint, the engineer left through the door, apologizing. King Muhammad locked it after he left.

"As I was saying, the satellite I need you to build isn't a surveillance satellite. I need you to build a weapon."

"What? What kind of weapon would we have to send into space?"

"A kinetic bombardment satellite."

Fahad swallowed hard. "Those only exist in science fiction."

"But it is more than possible to make. Just attach large tungsten rods to a satellite on a decoupling mechanism, put a small thrust module on the back for atmospheric reentry, and attach fins to the rear for small course adjustments when back in the atmosphere. A Raspberry Pi with a small radio receiver could even be used to control it remotely. I need ten rods mounted on this satellite."

"So we could make one. What would we even need with such a devastating weapon?!"

"A last resort. Should ISIS take one of our cities, or one of our oil fields, and we can't take it back. . . Well, we could deal a devastating blow with such a devastating weapon."

"I see."

"I wish I had a better solution. I wish I could solve this with diplomacy. But ISIS only listens to violence. This would be a shout too loud for them to ignore."

Fahad continued staring at the king.

"I need you to build this. Saudi Arabia needs you to build this. Your fellow Muslims need you to build this. The world needs you to build this."

So I'm preparing to make my own website like http://politicalcompass.org where you select answers to questions and some more concise statistics on where you stand politically. The difference being that it would be based on this post I made a while ago, with a political triangle instead of that two-axis system. Also the questions are supposed to be strictly policy questions, and not the more vague and philosophical questions that the political compass uses.

Anyway, here's the questions I have so far on the survey:

http://pastebin.com/HeibzWxX

Some notes:

  • The hyphen before a line indicates a radio button multiple choice answer, you can only choose one of these.
  • An asterisk before a line indicates a checkbox type answer. You can check multiple of these in one question.
  • Lines another tab in after a multiple choice line (I really hope the formatting was preserved) indicate questions/options only available if you choose the above line.
  • The test will work in that there are two scores. There are "b" and "r" scores effectively referring to the blue and red areas of the triangle. The "b" more or less means authoritarian right, and the "r" refers to authoritarian left. A low score in both indicates libertarianism.
  • Every question has an answer that adds no "r" or "b" points, making it the libertarian answer.
  • Answers that add both points indicate generic authoritarianism without a specific left or right leaning.

If you have any questions you'd like to see added, please let me know. I hope to be posting another topic this weekend with the website.
